Note::TexAccessor::simplify_roots¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::simplify_roots() const

Canonicalize Root Syntax While Retaining TeX¶

simplify_roots() normalizes complete square-root and indexed-root calls to \sqrt{radicand} and \sqrt[index]{radicand}. It removes whitespace between the command and its groups and trims only the outer edge of each group. Use it to obtain stable TeX source for comparison, caching, or later transforms. Use sqrt_pow() instead when roots should become explicit powers.

The command name is exact and case-sensitive. An optional index must be a balanced bracket group, and the radicand must be a balanced brace group. Nested braces and nested roots are normalized recursively. Longer names, escaped spellings, starred forms, missing groups, and unbalanced calls are preserved rather than partially interpreted. The method does not evaluate a root or decide whether an index is mathematically valid.

The operation is out-of-place, idempotent, shape preserving, and Text-only. Undefined state propagates. Runtime is linear in source bytes with recursion proportional to root nesting depth.

Example 1: Square, Indexed, And Nested Roots¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\sqrt [ 3 ] { a + \sqrt { {b} } })",
    R"(\sqrt { x } + \sqrt[ n + 1 ]{ y })"});
std::cout << source.tex().simplify_roots() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["\\sqrt[3]{a + \\sqrt{{b}}}", "\\sqrt{x} + \\sqrt[n + 1]{y}"]

Example 2: Ambiguous Source Is Preserved¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    R"(\sqrted{x} \\sqrt{x} \sqrt[3]oops \sqrt{broken)");
std::cout << source.tex().simplify_roots() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"\\sqrted{x} \\\\sqrt{x} \\sqrt[3]oops \\sqrt{broken"

Example 3: Higher-Rank Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\sqrt {a})", "plain",
                             R"(\sqrt [4] {b})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().simplify_roots() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["\\sqrt{a}", "plain"],
  ["\\sqrt[4]{b}", ""]
]

Example 4: Idempotence And Type Boundaries¶

const auto once = pluss::make_note(R"(\sqrt {x})").tex().simplify_roots();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent="
          << ((once == once.tex().simplify_roots()).all().bool_item())
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().simplify_roots().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().simplify_roots();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false
Int64: rejected
